description_full: Penguin Solutions, Inc., an AI factory platform company, designs, builds, deploys, and manages data centers for enterprises, sovereign AI initiatives, and neocloud providers in the United States, China, Europe, Mexico, and internationally. Its full-stack AI factory platform combines infrastructure software, advanced memory, compute systems, end-to-end services, and industry-leading partner technologies to help customers accelerate AI adoption, optimize token economics, and maximize return on AI investments. The company operates through three segments: Advanced Computing, Integrated Memory, and Optimized LED. The Advanced Computing segment provides AI and high-performance computing solutions under the Penguin Solutions and Penguin Computing brands, including ClusterWareAI AI factory operating system software, MemoryAI data center and AI inference solutions, ComputeAI GPU and CPU computing systems, and OriginAI reference architectures. It also offers high-availability and fault-tolerant computing solutions under Stratus brand. The Integrated Memory segment designs, develops, and delivers advanced memory and storage solutions that for AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, networking, and enterprise applications. It offers specialty memory and storage products under the SMART Modular Technologies product brand, including dynamic random access memory modules, solid-state and flash storage solutions, and CXL-based memory expansion technologies. This segment also provides customized supply chain planning and execution solutions. The Optimized LED segment offers application-optimized LED products that enable its customers to develop and market LED-based products for lighting, video displays and specialty lighting applications. The company was formerly known as SMART Global Holdings, Inc. and changed its name to Penguin Solutions, Inc. in October 2024. Penguin Solutions, Inc. was founded in 1988 and is headquartered in Fremont, California.

financial_summary: Penguin Solutions, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.4B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 24% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $163M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at +12.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 3.0% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.99).

At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 6.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.04, a backlog worth 9% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 52%.
